mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous year same month for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over two months signals a housing demand-driven slowdown with weakening overall demand, which depresses consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 1% month-over-month while GDPC1 decreases month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of such co-movement episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over two months indicates labor market saturation without wage growth, which reduces inflationary pressure and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent low FEDFUNDS rate below 1% for more than one year, combined with rising CPIAUCSL above 3% for six consecutive months, signals accommodative policy with rising inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >12 months AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions hold.

mechanism_narrative: A steady increase in RSAFS above trend for three consecutive months signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > trend for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above trend for three months.
